q:
Possible complications in the evolution of a colon cancer
a. diastatic perforation
b. intussusception
c. stenosis
d. acute diverticulitis
e. colo-vesical fistula
a:
a, c, e
✅ Correct: A, B, C, E
—————————————————————————
✅ A. Correct. Colon cancer may cause diastatic perforation due to obstruction and proximal colonic distension.
✅ B. Correct. A tumor can act as a lead point for intussusception.
✅ C. Correct. Progressive luminal narrowing from tumor growth causes stenosis.
❌ D. Incorrect. Acute diverticulitis is not a complication of colon cancer itself.
✅ E. Correct. Invasive sigmoid tumors may form a colo-vesical fistula.
—————————————————————————

—————————————————————————

Typical complications:

  • Obstruction (most common)

  • Perforation (tumor or proximal bowel)

  • Bleeding → iron-deficiency anemia

  • Fistulas (e.g., colovesical, colovaginal)

  • Local invasion (abdominal wall, bladder, ureter, small bowel)

  • Metastasis (liver, lung, peritoneum → ascites, SBO)

  • Hypercoagulability (paraneoplastic)

Intussusception?

  • Not a typical complication.

  • But colon cancer can cause adult intussusception as a malignant lead point (important but uncommon).
